messages:
kai: hey team, acme reported a sharp p95/p99 latency regression after we onboarded rwd-long-kv-13b-v2 yesterday. p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99 is hitting 2.7s. they say it started around 11:10 UTC. attaching their sample call and timings they sent.

acme-cust-sre: here's what we sent (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-long-kv-13b-v2","input":"<~5k char user prompt>", "max_tokens":512, "stream":false}'
```
Response times measured client-side: 95th=1.2s, 99th=2.7s. token_count returned by the API: 4096. same prompt on rwd-long-kv-13b-v1: 95th=240ms.

kai: thanks. joel, can you check model/tokenizer diffs from v1->v2? suspect tokenizer change or kv cache semantics.

joel: looking now. quick notes: v2 introduced special-token normalization (we replaced single-token CLS/SOT with multi-byte markers to support more languages). patch: commit f3a9b12. I also see we changed the padding/truncation routine to prefer right-pad to full 4096 when inputs include certain unicode sequences — could increase tokenized length for edge prompts.

ana: tagging ana (eng-runtime). if tokenized_len balloons, kv cache size and memory layout might cause repeated recompute/longer attention ops.

ana (ana): saw the thread. initial hypothesis: two issues coinciding: 1) tokenizer now expands some punctuation sequences into 2x tokens (so prompts that were ~2k tokens are now 3.8-4k), 2) we accidentally set KV_CACHE_TTL=0 in the v2 runtime config for dedicated pools, which disables prefix reuse across repeated short requests in the same session. combined effect: more tokens per request + no KV reuse => throughput collapse and higher tail latency.

kai: do we have repro locally? joel, can you share a minimal repro prompt and token counts?

joel: repro: the customer prompt includes consecutive emoji and invisible joiner chars. minimal example I used: \"Hello 👋‍♀️\n\nSummary: \"Lots of invisible joiners\"\n\"
Tokenization stats: v1 -> 2052 tokens, v2 -> 4048 tokens. took a screenshot of the token id stream.

joel: ran a local bench harness against rwd-long-kv-13b-v2 on a dev GPU: single-threaded cold-run latency for 512 decode tokens: 1.5s vs 230ms on v1. profile points to attention kernels and repeated kv cache warmup.

ana (ana): steps for temporary mitigations we can do immediately: 
- roll back tokenizer normalization for the affected model (quick toggle)
- set KV_CACHE_TTL back to 60s for the dedicated pool (allows reuse of prefixes)
- pin acme's workspace to rwd-long-kv-13b-v1 or rwd-mini-7b-longctx (fallback) until we stabilize v2
- enable dynamic batching override to lower max_batch_size for that model to reduce head-of-line impact

kai: can we apply those now as config changes without full model redeploy?

ana (ana): yes for TTL and batching via runtime flags. tokenizer toggle is in model-serving config; we can hot-swap the tokenizer binary in the model directory and restart the per-model worker (zero-downtime for other models).

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: change set #4321 (revert token-normalize, set KV_CACHE_TTL=60, set max_batch_size=8 for rwd-long-kv-13b-v2). approvers: @ana, @joel. ETA 12m.

joel: I pushed a tokenizer binary rollback to staging and ran the same client call: token_count returned -> 2056, p95=260ms, p99=410ms. good signal.

acme-cust-sre: thanks for the quick turnaround. can you also confirm billing/usage won't be double-charged due to repeated retries? we saw some extra requests from our side when timeouts happened.

kai: billing note: repeated retries are counted as separate calls. we'll review their logs and refund excess token usage for calls during the incident window. ops will coordinate.

ana (ana): deploy complete: change set #4321 applied to dedicated pool (rollout 100%). rolling poster-mortem in #incidents and linking to onboarding PR.

deploy-bot: rollout complete for change set #4321 (commit f3a9b12 -> reverted token-normalize).

joel: post-deploy validation: acme provided a 600-request synthetic run. before fix: 600 requests took ~18 minutes with many timeouts. after fix: 600 requests completed in ~3:10 with p95 ~270ms.

kai: next actions (owned): 
- joel: create a regression test that fuzzes unicode/invisible joiners and asserts token_count for new tokenizer doesn't grow more than 1.2x compared to baseline. add to onboarding CI.
- ana: add a runtime alert for sudden >=2x tokenized_len vs baseline per-customer for 1h.
- kai: handle customer refunds and communication (support playbook).

acme-cust-sre: appreciate the communication. we'll confirm on our side and reopen if anything else crops up.

joel: PR #987 (tokenizer normalization rework) will include better normalization maps and a canary flag. planning a phased rollout with canaries limited to 5% traffic and a token-growth monitor.

kai: great. I'll draft the support postmortem and link the PR/regen tests. closing this thread after postmortem posted. :thumbsup:
